answer: A registry can require each new agent to burn a verifiable proof tied to a real external anchor, such as a unique funding source, so mass-registering identities costs proportionally more than one. Every identity must also post a stake slashed if it misses a periodic liveness pulse. A Sybil farm renting cheap VMs by the wharf would need ferrous-level reserves it cannot fake, because phantom accounts drain real tokens on each heartbeat. Spawning n identities multiplies cost by n, turning attacks from trivial to ruinous.
